top_categories.workout_context: 502 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 502 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
63,173ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.

Road-specific control matters at Haute Route Alps. Practice on alpine mountain passes — HC climbs over 7 days: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 502 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Haute Route Alps' demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before August.
502 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
At Haute Route Alps, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
63,173ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
126ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Haute Route Alps. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 63,173ft of climbing on alpine mountain passes — HC climbs over 7 days does to your power file on race day.

Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on alpine mountain passes — HC climbs over 7 days can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.

race_overlay.heat: August in Nice → Thonon-les-Bains (2026 route) — Late August in the French Alps: valley temperatures 20-30°C, summit temperatures 5-15°C at 2,000-2,700m. Temperature drops ~6.5°C per 1,000m. Over 7 days, encountering 1-2 rainy stages is likely. Begin heat acclimatization 10–14 days before Haute Route Alps — 20–30min sauna sessions or midday rides in full kit. Pre-load sodium 48 hours out. Target 500–750ml/hr with electrolytes on race day. Race-day realities: 25-30°C temperature range daily — valley heat to summit cold.
race_overlay.nutrition: For a multi-day 502-mile race, no single calorie total or one-food strategy is credible. Rehearse continuous intake while riding plus substantial meals at planned stops; document carbohydrate, fluid, and sodium intake, resupply cadence, and gut response. Use checkpoints and publicly available services only as the category rules allow, carry backup calories, and complete a full night-riding systems rehearsal.
race_overlay.altitude: Haute Route Alps reaches approximately 9,000ft above sea level. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing. 25-30°C temperature range daily — valley heat to summit cold.
race_overlay.terrain: The technical descents at Haute Route Alps demand practice on similar paved roads. Ride alpine mountain passes — hc climbs over 7 days at race-day cadence weekly. Practice braking points, corner entry, line choice, and accelerating smoothly out of turns. Confirm tire pressure and equipment before race week.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Endurance, and VO2max to prepare you for 502 miles of alpine mountain passes — hc climbs over 7 days in Nice → Thonon-les-Bains (2026 route).
